findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/playbook-runtime-memory.ts:21 duplicate-definition: local `type FinishDecision = 'captured' | 'no-reusable-lesson' | 'defer-with-reason';` was NOT deleted when finishDecisionPath was moved to core/playbook-runtime-memory.ts (which now exports its own identical `FinishDecision` type at line 892, plus `FinishDecisionRecord`). The plan/checklist explicitly frame this refactor as single-source-of-truth (CHK-003 edge:1: 'single source of truth for the path, no duplicate definitions'), and the sibling function finishDecisionPath WAS correctly deleted from handlers and re-imported from core, but the type alias it is paired with was left as an independent, unimported local copy instead of importing FinishDecision from core/playbook-runtime-memory.js. Two structurally-identical but textually-independent type definitions now exist for the same concept; if the core union is ever extended the handlers copy will silently drift out of sync since nothing ties them together. Not a compile error today (TS structural typing hides it), but it is exactly the dead/duplicate-code residue this refactor was supposed to eliminate.
findings.resolvedReason: Imported FinishDecision as a type-only import from core/playbook-runtime-memory.js instead of redefining it locally; removed the duplicate local type alias. Rebuilt (tsc clean).

findings.desc: checklist.json CHK-005:adversarial:0 (intentRef) evidence: verification command is `git diff main...HEAD -- docs/requirements/decisions/playbook-runtime-memory-consumption-execution-plan.md`, selector `"missing decision is visible in runbook/advisory output"` (no +/- diff-line prefix). The gate mechanism (packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:645, `selectorMatched = run.output.includes(pinSelector)`) is a raw substring match over the entire diff output, so it cannot distinguish the phrase appearing on a preserved context line from it appearing on a removed `-` line. If the original M8 advisory text had actually been deleted (the exact adversarial scenario this intent claims to test: user explicitly flagged losing/deleting the original rationale as an adversarial failure mode), this same command+selector would still report pass, because a git-diff deletion still contains the phrase as substring text on the `-` line. The evidence note correctly reasons that todays diff has zero removed lines, but that reasoning is human-authored prose, not something the pinned command mechanically verifies going forward. A robust version of the same claim already exists at CHK-005:edge:0 (readFileSync(...).includes(...) against final file content) -- that pattern was not reused for adversarial:0.

checklist.json CHK-006:happy:1, CHK-006:edge:1, and CHK-006:adversarial:0 (intentRefs) all bind to the same command `git diff main...HEAD -- docs/requirements/decisions/dev-memory.md` with selectors lacking a +/- diff-line prefix (happy:1 and adversarial:0 use the identical selector text). Same non-discriminating mechanism as the CHK-005 finding: packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:645s `run.output.includes(pinSelector)` matches the phrase whether it sits on a preserved context line or a removed `-` line, so none of these three checks can mechanically prove not deleted vs deleted. Unlike CHK-005 (which has a companion CHK-005:edge:0 readFileSync-based final-content check for the same claim), none of CHK-006s 9 verificationEvidence entries independently re-verifies via final-file content (readFileSync(...).includes(...)) that the original Non-Goal bullet (Dev-memory entries are NOT surfaced in `lattice validate` output or gate checks.) still exists in the current dev-memory.md -- the only evidence for that specific not deleted claim is this weak diff-substring pattern, duplicated identically across happy:1 and adversarial:0.
